Trump’s approval among white registered voters has moved underwater in six states he won in 2024, according to the Civiqs tracker.  
  
Kentucky and Texas saw especially large swings, with Trump’s net approval dropping 32 points in Kentucky and 30 points in Texas between Jan. 20, 2025, and Sept. 24, 2026.  
  
That does not tell us how these voters will vote in November. But it does show a significant change in approval within a demographic group Trump won by a wide margin in 2024. [...] Sources: Civiqs | Newsweek | Pew Research Center | Washington Post

A September 2026 YouGov survey found that only 23% of independents approve of Trump’s job as president, compared with 79% of Republicans and 2% of Democrats. This continues a steady drop in independents’ approval of Trump throughout his second term.

Independents have also soured on Trump’s handling of the economy, with 73% in a September Fox News poll saying that Trump has made the economy worse, a sentiment also expressed by 95% of Democrats and 26% of Republicans.
